- [Yuri Matiyasevich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Matiyasevich) was able to show that the Fibonacci numbers can be defined by a [Diophantine equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diophantine_equation), which led to [his solving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matiyasevich's_theorem) [Hilbert's tenth problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert's_tenth_problem).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-71)
- The Fibonacci numbers are also an example of a [complete sequence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complete_sequence). This means that every positive integer can be written as a sum of Fibonacci numbers, where any one number is used once at most.
- Moreover, every positive integer can be written in a unique way as the sum of *one or more* distinct Fibonacci numbers in such a way that the sum does not include any two consecutive Fibonacci numbers. This is known as [Zeckendorf's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeckendorf's_theorem), and a sum of Fibonacci numbers that satisfies these conditions is called a Zeckendorf representation. The Zeckendorf representation of a number can be used to derive its [Fibonacci coding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_coding).
- Starting with 5, every second Fibonacci number is the length of the [hypotenuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypotenuse) of a [right triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_triangle) with integer sides, or in other words, the largest number in a [Pythagorean triple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythagorean_triple), obtained from the formula     (  F  n    F  n + 3    )  2   + ( 2  F  n + 1    F  n + 2    )  2   =    F  2 n + 3     2   .   {\displaystyle (F_{n}F_{n+3})^{2}+(2F_{n+1}F_{n+2})^{2}={F_{2n+3}}^{2}.}   The sequence of Pythagorean triangles obtained from this formula has sides of lengths (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (16,30,34), (39,80,89), ... . The middle side of each of these triangles is the sum of the three sides of the preceding triangle.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-72)
- The [Fibonacci cube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_cube) is an [undirected graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undirected_graph) with a Fibonacci number of nodes that has been proposed as a [network topology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_topology) for [parallel computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_computing).
- Fibonacci numbers appear in the [ring lemma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_lemma), used to prove connections between the [circle packing theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_packing_theorem) and [conformal maps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conformal_map).[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-73)

### Computer science

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fibonacci_sequence&action=edit&section=33)] [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Fibonacci_Tree_6.svg/330px-Fibonacci_Tree_6.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fibonacci_Tree_6.svg)Fibonacci tree of height 6. [Balance factors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AVL_tree#Balance_factor) green; heights red.
The keys in the left spine are Fibonacci numbers.
- The Fibonacci numbers are important in [computational run-time analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analysis_of_algorithms) of [Euclid's algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclidean_algorithm) to determine the [greatest common divisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest_common_divisor) of two integers: the worst case input for this algorithm is a pair of consecutive Fibonacci numbers.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-74)
- Fibonacci numbers are used in a polyphase version of the [merge sort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merge_sort) algorithm in which an unsorted list is divided into two lists whose lengths correspond to sequential Fibonacci numbers—by dividing the list so that the two parts have lengths in the approximate proportion φ. A tape-drive implementation of the [polyphase merge sort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyphase_merge_sort) was described in *[The Art of Computer Programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Art_of_Computer_Programming)*.
- A Fibonacci tree is a [binary tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_tree) whose child trees (recursively) differ in [height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_height) by exactly 1. So it is an [AVL tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AVL_tree), and one with the fewest nodes for a given height—the "thinnest" AVL tree. These trees have a number of vertices that is a Fibonacci number minus one, an important fact in the analysis of AVL trees.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-75)
- Fibonacci numbers are used by some [pseudorandom number generators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudorandom_number_generator).
- Fibonacci numbers arise in the analysis of the [Fibonacci heap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_heap) data structure.
- A one-dimensional optimization method, called the [Fibonacci search technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_search_technique), uses Fibonacci numbers.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-76)
- The Fibonacci number series is used for optional [lossy compression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lossy_compression) in the [IFF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interchange_File_Format) [8SVX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8SVX) audio file format used on [Amiga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amiga) computers. The number series [compands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companding) the original audio wave similar to logarithmic methods such as [μ-law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CE%9C-law).[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-77)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-78)
- Some Agile teams use a modified series called the "Modified Fibonacci Series" in [planning poker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planning_poker), as an estimation tool. Planning Poker is a formal part of the [Scaled Agile Framework](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scaled_agile_framework).[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-79)
- [Fibonacci coding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_coding)
- [Negafibonacci coding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negafibonacci_coding)
- In [topological quantum computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological_quantum_computer), quasi-particles called [Fibonacci anyons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_anyons) could be used for universal quantum computation. The dimension of the [Hilbert space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_formulation_of_quantum_mechanics) describing n Fibonacci anyons is the Fibonacci number *F**n*+1.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-80)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-81)

### Nature

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fibonacci_sequence&action=edit&section=34)] Further information: [Patterns in nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patterns_in_nature) See also: [Golden ratio § Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_ratio#Nature) [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/FibonacciChamomile.PNG/250px-FibonacciChamomile.PNG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FibonacciChamomile.PNG)[Yellow chamomile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_chamomile) head showing the arrangement in 21 (blue) and 13 (cyan) spirals. Such arrangements involving consecutive Fibonacci numbers appear in a wide variety of plants.

Fibonacci sequences appear in biological settings,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-82) such as branching in trees, [arrangement of leaves on a stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllotaxis), the fruitlets of a [pineapple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pineapple),[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-83) the flowering of [artichoke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artichoke), the leaves of the spiral aloe[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-84) (Aloe polyphylla), the arrangement of a [pine cone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine_cone),[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-85) and the family tree of [honeybees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeybee).[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-86)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-87) [Kepler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kepler) pointed out the presence of the Fibonacci sequence in nature, using it to explain the ([golden ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_ratio)-related) [pentagonal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentagon) form of some flowers.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-FOOTNOTELivio2003110-88) Field [daisies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leucanthemum_vulgare) most often have petals in counts of Fibonacci numbers.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-FOOTNOTELivio2003112%E2%80%9313-89) In 1830, [Karl Friedrich Schimper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Friedrich_Schimper) and [Alexander Braun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Braun) discovered that the [parastichies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parastichy) (spiral [phyllotaxis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllotaxis)) of plants were frequently expressed as fractions involving Fibonacci numbers.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-90)

[Przemysław Prusinkiewicz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Przemys%C5%82aw_Prusinkiewicz) advanced the idea that real instances can in part be understood as the expression of certain algebraic constraints on [free groups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_group), specifically as certain [Lindenmayer grammars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L-system).[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-91)

 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/SunflowerModel.svg/250px-SunflowerModel.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SunflowerModel.svg)Illustration of Vogel's model for *n* = 1 ... 500

A model for the pattern of [florets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floret) in the head of a [sunflower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower) was proposed by [Helmut Vogel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Vogel?action=edit&redlink=1) [[de](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut%20Vogel%20(Physiker))] in 1979.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-92) This has the form

θ =    2 π   φ  2     n ,   r = c   n     {\displaystyle \theta ={\frac {2\pi }{\varphi ^{2}}}n,\ r=c{\sqrt {n}}}

where n is the index number of the floret and c is a constant scaling factor; the florets thus lie on [Fermat's spiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat's_spiral). The divergence [angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angle), approximately 137.51°, is the [golden angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_angle), dividing the circle in the golden ratio. Because this ratio is irrational, no floret has a neighbor at exactly the same angle from the center, so the florets pack efficiently. Because the rational approximations to the golden ratio are of the form *F*( *j*):*F*( *j* + 1), the nearest neighbors of floret number n are those at *n* ± *F*( *j*) for some index j, which depends on r, the distance from the center. Sunflowers and similar flowers most commonly have spirals of florets in clockwise and counter-clockwise directions in the amount of adjacent Fibonacci numbers,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-FOOTNOTELivio2003112-93) typically counted by the outermost range of radii.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-94)

Fibonacci numbers also appear in the ancestral pedigrees of [bees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bee) (which are [haplodiploids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haplodiploid)), according to the following rules:

- If an egg is laid but not fertilized, it produces a male (or [drone bee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drone_(bee)) in honeybees).
- If, however, an egg is fertilized, it produces a female.

Thus, a male bee always has one parent, and a female bee has two. If one traces the pedigree of any male bee (1 bee), he has 1 parent (1 bee), 2 grandparents, 3 great-grandparents, 5 great-great-grandparents, and so on. This sequence of numbers of parents is the Fibonacci sequence. The number of ancestors at each level, *F**n*, is the number of female ancestors, which is *F**n*−1, plus the number of male ancestors, which is *F**n*−2.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-95)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-96) This is under the unrealistic assumption that the ancestors at each level are otherwise unrelated.

 [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/X_chromosome_ancestral_line_Fibonacci_sequence.svg/330px-X_chromosome_ancestral_line_Fibonacci_sequence.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:X_chromosome_ancestral_line_Fibonacci_sequence.svg)The number of possible ancestors on the X chromosome inheritance line at a given ancestral generation follows the Fibonacci sequence. (After Hutchison, L. "Growing the Family Tree: The Power of DNA in Reconstructing Family Relationships".[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-xcs-97))

It has similarly been noticed that the number of possible ancestors on the human [X chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_chromosome) inheritance line at a given ancestral generation also follows the Fibonacci sequence.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-xcs-97) A male individual has an X chromosome, which he received from his mother, and a [Y chromosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y_chromosome), which he received from his father. The male counts as the "origin" of his own X chromosome (     F  1   = 1   {\displaystyle F_{1}=1}  ), and at his parents' generation, his X chromosome came from a single parent (     F  2   = 1   {\displaystyle F_{2}=1}  ). The male's mother received one X chromosome from her mother (the son's maternal grandmother), and one from her father (the son's maternal grandfather), so two grandparents contributed to the male descendant's X chromosome (     F  3   = 2   {\displaystyle F_{3}=2}  ). The maternal grandfather received his X chromosome from his mother, and the maternal grandmother received X chromosomes from both of her parents, so three great-grandparents contributed to the male descendant's X chromosome (     F  4   = 3   {\displaystyle F_{4}=3}  ). Five great-great-grandparents contributed to the male descendant's X chromosome (     F  5   = 5   {\displaystyle F_{5}=5}  ), etc. (This assumes that all ancestors of a given descendant are independent, but if any genealogy is traced far enough back in time, ancestors begin to appear on multiple lines of the genealogy, until eventually a [population founder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founder_effect) appears on all lines of the genealogy.)

### Other

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fibonacci_sequence&action=edit&section=35)]
- In [optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optics), when a beam of light shines at an angle through two stacked transparent plates of different materials of different [refractive indexes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refractive_index), it may reflect off three surfaces: the top, middle, and bottom surfaces of the two plates. The number of different beam paths that have k reflections, for *k* > 1, is the k-th Fibonacci number. (However, when *k* = 1, there are three reflection paths, not two, one for each of the three surfaces.)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-FOOTNOTELivio200398%E2%80%9399-98)
- [Fibonacci retracement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_retracement) levels are widely used in [technical analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_analysis) for financial market trading.
- Since the [conversion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_of_units) factor 1.609344 for miles to kilometers is close to the golden ratio, the decomposition of distance in miles into a sum of Fibonacci numbers becomes nearly the kilometer sum when the Fibonacci numbers are replaced by their successors. This method amounts to a [radix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radix) 2 number [register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Processor_register) in [golden ratio base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_ratio_base) φ being shifted. To convert from kilometers to miles, shift the register down the Fibonacci sequence instead.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-99)
- The measured values of voltages and currents in the infinite resistor chain circuit (also called the [resistor ladder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resistor_ladder) or infinite series-parallel circuit) follow the Fibonacci sequence. The intermediate results of adding the alternating series and parallel resistances yields fractions composed of consecutive Fibonacci numbers. The equivalent resistance of the entire circuit equals the golden ratio.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-100)
- Brasch et al. 2012 show how a generalized Fibonacci sequence also can be connected to the field of [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics).[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-Brasch_et_al._2012-101) In particular, it is shown how a generalized Fibonacci sequence enters the control function of finite-horizon dynamic optimisation problems with one state and one control variable. The procedure is illustrated in an example often referred to as the Brock–Mirman economic growth model.
- [Mario Merz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Merz) included the Fibonacci sequence in some of his artworks beginning in 1970.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-FOOTNOTELivio2003176-102)
- [Joseph Schillinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Schillinger) (1895–1943) developed [a system of composition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schillinger_System) which uses Fibonacci intervals in some of its melodies; he viewed these as the musical counterpart to the elaborate harmony evident within nature.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-FOOTNOTELivio2003193-103) See also [Golden ratio § Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_ratio#Music).
- In [software development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development), Fibonacci numbers are often used by [agile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agile_management) teams operating under the [Scrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scrum_(software_development)) framework to size their [product backlog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_backlog) items.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibonacci_sequence#cite_note-104)
